## claude.ai Dropbox
# Claude App MCP LLM Boot Instructions

You are the assistant for Dropbox's Claude App MCP server. Your goal is to help users complete Dropbox tasks quickly and correctly while minimizing friction.

## Customer Use Cases

This app is best at helping users do these Dropbox workflows:

- Browse folder contents and paginate through large directories.
- Find files quickly using plain-language search terms and then open files with follow-on tools.
- Inspect file metadata (size, type, timestamps, IDs, sharing context).
- Check signed-in Dropbox identity, team/account context, and namespace-root context.
- Read text content from supported files up to 5 MiB, and provide a usable Dropbox link even when text extraction fails.
- Generate single-use temporary download links when the user explicitly needs direct file download URLs.
- Generate file previews with thumbnail and "open in Dropbox" experiences.
- Create folders in the right destination before saving artifacts.
- Create new text files directly in Dropbox.
- Create share links for files/folders and return the effective sharing settings.
- Inspect and list existing shared links.
- List, inspect, and create Dropbox file requests.
- Move, rename, copy, and delete Dropbox files/folders after explicit confirmation.
- Check the status of long-running move, copy, and delete jobs.

When users ask "what can you do?", summarize these use cases in plain language before taking action.

## Not Supported (Do Not Advertise)

- Editing or overwriting existing file content in place.
- Saving URL-hosted files directly into Dropbox.
- Uploading local/binary artifacts via `upload_file`.
- Permanent file deletion or wipe workflows. `delete` moves items to the user's Dropbox "Deleted files" area only.
- Reliable text extraction for supported files via `fetch`; extraction may still fail for some files, in which case the tool error may include a usable link.
- E-signature initiation or signing workflows.
- Actions outside Dropbox content management and sharing.

## devonthink
CRITICAL — Database package safety: DEVONthink databases are stored as packages (.dtBase2) or sparse images (.dtSparse, .dtArchive). Never modify, rename, move, or delete files inside a database package directly via the filesystem. All record and content operations must go through this MCP server or, as a fallback, via AppleScript. Direct filesystem manipulation will corrupt the database and cause irreversible data loss.

Batch operations: Use the uuids array parameter instead of sequential single-record calls for tag, update, move, trash, duplicate, replicate, and export operations. Batch mode is faster, reduces round trips, and returns a summary with succeeded/failed counts.

Avoiding duplicates: Use lookup_records (by name, URL, path, filename, or comment) before create_record to check whether a record already exists.

Content editing: Prefer update_record_content with mode append or insert over replace for large documents. Replace mode requires sending the entire new content and risks accidental data loss if the content is incomplete.

Group hierarchies: Use create_group_path to create nested group structures in a single call (like mkdir -p) rather than sequential create_record calls.

AI-powered tools: classify_record and find_similar_records use DEVONthink's built-in AI algorithms and proprietary training data — they provide organizational suggestions that complement, not duplicate, your own capabilities.

Record enrichment: resolve_doi_metadata and resolve_book_metadata can enrich existing records with bibliographic metadata by passing the record's uuid — there is no need to create a new record.

AI exclusion: Records marked as excluded from AI access (excludeFromChat) are protected in two ways. (1) Input protection: any tool that receives such a record's UUID as an argument refuses to operate on it and returns an error. I have gathered enough. Here is the structured summary.

# Expense-Tracker Codebase Findings

## 1. How a "family" is represented

**Tables** (base schema in `supabase/migrations/20251010000319_remote_schema.sql`):

`families` (lines 95-100):
- `id` uuid PK (default `gen_random_uuid()`)
- `name` text (nullable — auto-created families are created with `name = null`)
- `created_at` timestamptz NOT NULL
- Also a `created_by` uuid column (referenced by `ensure_default_family()` at line 194; added elsewhere in the schema/policies)

`family_members` (lines 104-139) — composite PK `(family_id, user_id)`:
- `family_id` uuid → `families(id)` ON DELETE CASCADE
- `user_id` uuid → `auth.users(id)` ON DELETE CASCADE
- `status` text NOT NULL default `'active'`, CHECK in `('active','invited','removed')`
- `role` text (default `'member'`, added in `006_add_is_default_to_family_members.sql:32`; `ensure_default_family` inserts `'owner'`)
- `is_default` boolean (added in `006_...:20`, `NOT NULL default false`) — marks the user's default family

**TypeScript models:** There is no dedicated `src/lib/models/Family*.ts`. Family shapes live in:
- `src/lib/utils/familyMembers.ts:11` — `FamilyMember` type (`user_id, email, role, status, is_default`) + `decorateFamilyMembers()`
- `src/lib/utils/familyUtils.ts` — `getDefaultFamilyId()`, `getActiveFamilyIds()`, `getFamilyMembers()` (RPC)
- Test-only row types in `src/lib/tests/builders/testDatabase.ts:21` (`FamilyRow`, `FamilyMemberRow`)

## 2. Receipts

**Table** `receipts` — created in `supabase/migrations/001_init.sql:5-17`, extended by later migrations. Full field set is in the model `src/lib/models/Receipt.ts:1-19` (`ReceiptRow`).

**NOT NULL / required columns:**
- `id` uuid PK
- `user_id` uuid NOT NULL → `auth.users(id)` (`001_init.sql:7`)
- `created_at` timestamptz NOT NULL
- `is_duplicate` boolean NOT NULL default false (`008:...`), `suspicious_date` boolean NOT NULL default false (`011_add_suspicious_date_flag.sql`)

**Nullable columns:** `transaction_date`, `total_amount`, `tax`, `merchant_name`, `credit_card_name`, `credit_card_last_4`, `currency`, `exchange_rate_to_cad` (added `20260405`), `matched_transaction_id` (added `008`), `split_group_id` (`20260228`), `original_filename` (`20260607`), and `family_id` (added `20251010...:139`, FK to families ON DELETE SET NULL).

**Storage image field:** `receipt_image_path` text — and it **is nullable** (`001_init.sql:8`; `Receipt.ts:5` typed `string | null`). It stores the object path in the private `receipts` storage bucket; the path convention is `{user_id}/...` (first path segment is the owner's uid, used by storage RLS).

## 3. How "expenses" are computed

CLAUDE.md's claim is **confirmed**. Expenses are a *derived view*, not a table: `receipts` ⨝ `expense_categories` ⨝ `categories` (1:1 per receipt).

- Service: `src/lib/services/ExpenseService.ts`. `Expense` interface at line 22; the join query is `buildExpenseQuery()` at `ExpenseService.ts:154-190` — PostgREST embed `receipts → expense_categories (category_id, categorization_source) → categories (name, color)`.
- `mapReceiptRowToExpense()` (line ~195) flattens each receipt row into one `Expense`. `getExpenses()` (line 99) pages 1000 rows at a time and relies on **RLS** (no explicit `user_id` filter) for access.
- Migration `010_expense_categorization.sql` documents the design ("Expenses are derived views from receipts, not separate entities").

## 4. Transactions

**Table** `transactions` — `supabase/migrations/007_transactions_table.sql:2-15`. Model: `src/lib/models/Transaction.ts:3` (`TransactionRow`).

Key fields:
- `id` uuid PK
- `family_id` uuid NOT NULL → `families(id)` ON DELETE CASCADE (transactions are **family-scoped**, not user-scoped)
- `transaction_date` date NOT NULL
- `vendor_name` text NOT NULL
- `amount` numeric NOT NULL (no sign constraint in schema; stored as-is from CSV import)
- `credit_card_type` text NOT NULL (enum in `Transaction.ts:33` — PC Financial, Amex, RBC, TD, Simplii, EQ, Wealth Simple)
- `excluded` boolean NOT NULL default false — originally named `ignored`, renamed in `012_rename_ignored_to_excluded.sql`; means "excluded from reconciliation"
- `created_at`, `updated_at` timestamptz
- A `status` CHECK was added in `20260111000004_add_status_check_to_transactions.sql`
- Unique index on `(family_id, transaction_date, vendor_name, amount, credit_card_type)` created in `007` but later **dropped** in `20260419_drop_transactions_unique_index.sql`

**Matching to receipts:** the link lives on the receipt side — `receipts.matched_transaction_id` uuid → `transactions(id)` ON DELETE SET NULL (`008_add_receipt_transaction_matching.sql`).

## 5. Categories & expense_categories

Both defined in `supabase/migrations/010_expense_categorization.sql`:

`categories` (line 26): `id` PK, `user_id` NOT NULL→auth.users, `name` varchar(100) NOT NULL, `color` varchar(7) nullable, timestamps. Unique on `(user_id, lower(name))`. (Later migrated to family-scope by `20260111000001_migrate_categories_to_family_scope.sql`; test `CategoryRow` uses `family_id`.)

`expense_categories` (line 48) — the join table, **PK is `receipt_id`** (enforces 1:1 receipt↔category):
- `receipt_id` uuid PK → `receipts(id)` ON DELETE CASCADE
- `category_id` uuid → `categories(id)` ON DELETE SET NULL (nullable)
- `categorization_source` varchar(10) NOT NULL CHECK in `('manual','auto')`
- timestamps

`vendor_category_rules` (line 68): `user_id`, `vendor_pattern`, `category_id` — auto-categorization rules.

**How a receipt gets categorized:** `ExpenseService.assignCategory(receiptId, categoryId, source)` (`ExpenseService.ts:240`) does an `upsert` into `expense_categories` with `onConflict: 'receipt_id'` (manual overrides auto). Auto-assignment path: `ReceiptService.ts:368` calls `expenseService.assignCategory(receipt.id, vendorRule.category_id, 'auto')` when a vendor rule matches. No models file for these; row types only in `testDatabase.ts` (`CategoryRow`, `VendorCategoryRuleRow`).

## 6. Seed / sample / fixture data

**No production seed data mechanism exists.**
- `supabase/config.toml:58-63` declares `[db.seed] sql_paths = ["./seed.sql"]`, but **`supabase/seed.sql` does not exist** (default template config, unused).
- No `seed`/`sample`/`demo`/`fixture` npm script in `package.json` (scripts are only dev/build/test/lint).
- Fixtures found are all **test-only / unit-test scoped**, not DB seeders:
  - `src/lib/tests/fixtures/fetchMock.ts`, `src/lib/tests/fixtures/supabaseMock.ts` (mocks)
  - `src/lib/tests/builders/testDatabase.ts` (hand-written typed schema for integration tests — types families/family_members/receipts/categories but inserts nothing by itself)
  - `src/lib/utils/receiptDateCorrection.fixtures.ts`, `src/lib/components/DataTableFixture.svelte`, `e2e/demo.test.ts`, `src/demo.spec.ts`
- No test factory that seeds real families/receipts into a running DB; tests use the Supabase mock or the in-memory typed client.

## 7. Real signup flow & how a family is created

There is **no signup/register route** — only login. `src/routes/login/+page.svelte:17` calls `supabase.auth.signInWithPassword(...)`; there's no `+page.server.ts` and no `signUp()` call anywhere in `src/`. (Users appear to be provisioned externally / invite-based.)

Family creation is **lazy and DB-driven**, not done in an app route:
- Trigger function `set_receipt_family_id()` (`20251010...:149`) fires before insert on `receipts`; if `family_id` is null it calls `ensure_default_family()`.
- `ensure_default_family()` (SECURITY DEFINER; `005_fix_ensure_default_family_service_role.sql:5` and `20251010...:159`): finds the caller's active default membership; if none, **inserts a new `families` row (`created_by = uid`) and a `family_members` row (`role='owner', status='active', is_default=true`)**. This is the single place a family + membership get created.
- Ties to `auth.users`: `family_members.user_id` FK → `auth.users(id)`; the function keys everything off `auth.uid()` (or `request.jwt.claims->>'sub'` when invoked via the service-role RPC `insert_receipt_with_context`, `003`/`20260717`).
- Default categories seeded per-user via `create_default_categories(p_user_id)` (`010_...`) — a SECURITY DEFINER function, not wired to an auth trigger in these migrations.

## 8. RLS

RLS is enabled on all domain tables and is **family-membership scoped, keyed on `auth.uid()`** (plus legacy user_id scoping on categories/vendor_rules).

- **receipts:** RLS enabled in `001_init.sql:19`. Original policies were `user_id = auth.uid()`; hardened to family-scoped in `20260717_security_remediation_chain.sql` — insert/update policies now require `EXISTS(family_members fm WHERE fm.family_id = receipts.family_id AND fm.user_id = auth.uid())` (fixing a tautological check; lines 85-130), with a `family_id IS NULL AND auth.uid()=user_id` fallback.
- **transactions:** `007_transactions_table.sql:20-71` — all four policies gated on `EXISTS(family_members fm WHERE fm.family_id = transactions.family_id AND fm.user_id = auth.uid())`.
- **families / family_members:** policies in `20251010...:306-380`; recursion issues fixed by `20260113_fix_family_members_recursion.sql`, `20260114_simple_family_members_policy.sql`, and `20260717_...` (R5/F1) which replaced world-readable policies with membership-scoped SELECT via a SECURITY DEFINER helper and removed the open self-insert policy. Member listing goes through `get_family_members()` RPC (`20260719_get_family_members_rpc.sql`).
- **categories / expense_categories / vendor_category_rules:** RLS in `010_expense_categorization.sql:88-104` — `categories`/`vendor_rules` use `auth.uid() = user_id`; `expense_categories` uses `receipt_id IN (SELECT id FROM receipts WHERE user_id = auth.uid())`. RLS re-scoped by `20260111000001/2/3` (family-scope migrations, incl. `20260111000003_fix_expense_categories_rls.sql`).
- **Storage (`receipts` bucket):** `20260225_secure_receipts_storage.sql` makes the bucket private; SELECT allows any active family member to read files owned by a co-member (owner uid = first path segment), while INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE remain restricted to the owner's own `{auth.uid()}/` folder.
- Additional lockdown: `20260717_security_remediation_chain.sql` and `20260718_fix_f3_revoke_anon.sql` (revokes anon access).

**Key policy files:** `001_init.sql`, `007_transactions_table.sql`, `010_expense_categorization.sql`, `20251010000319_remote_schema.sql`, `20260111000003_fix_expense_categories_rls.sql`, `20260113_fix_family_members_recursion.sql`, `20260114_simple_family_members_policy.sql`, `20260225_secure_receipts_storage.sql`, `20260717_security_remediation_chain.sql`, `20260718_fix_f3_revoke_anon.sql`, `20260719_get_family_members_rpc.sql`.

# Expense-Tracker Codebase Findings

## 1. How a "family" is represented

**Tables** (base schema in `supabase/migrations/20251010000319_remote_schema.sql`):

`families` (lines 95-100):
- `id` uuid PK (default `gen_random_uuid()`)
- `name` text (nullable — auto-created families are created with `name = null`)
- `created_at` timestamptz NOT NULL

`family_members` (lines 104-139) — composite PK `(family_id, user_id)`:
- `family_id` uuid → `families(id)` ON DELETE CASCADE
- `user_id` uuid → `auth.users(id)` ON DELETE CASCADE
- `status` text NOT NULL default `'active'`, CHECK in `('active','invited','removed')`
- `role` text (default `'member'`, added in `006_add_is_default_to_family_members.sql:32`; `ensure_default_family` inserts `'owner'`)

## 2. Receipts

**Table** `receipts` — created in `supabase/migrations/001_init.sql:5-17`, extended by later migrations. Full field set is in the model `src/lib/models/Receipt.ts:1-19` (`ReceiptRow`).

**NOT NULL / required columns:**
- `id` uuid PK
- `user_id` uuid NOT NULL → `auth.users(id)` (`001_init.sql:7`)
- `created_at` timestamptz NOT NULL
- `is_duplicate` boolean NOT NULL default false (`008:...`), `suspicious_date` boolean NOT NULL default false (`011_add_suspicious_date_flag.sql`)

**Nullable columns:** `transaction_date`, `total_amount`, `tax`, `merchant_name`, `credit_card_name`, `credit_card_last_4`, `currency`, `exchange_rate_to_cad` (added `20260405`), `matched_transaction_id` (added `008`), `split_group_id` (`20260228`), `original_filename` (`20260607`), and `family_id` (added `20251010...:139`, FK to families ON DELETE SET NULL).

**Storage image field:** `receipt_image_path` text — and it **is nullable** (`001_init.sql:8`; `Receipt.ts:5` typed `string | null`). It stores the object path in the private `receipts` storage bucket; the path convention is `{user_id}/...` (first path segment is the owner's uid, used by storage RLS).

## 3. How "expenses" are computed

CLAUDE.md's claim is **confirmed**. Expenses are a *derived view*, not a table: `receipts` ⨝ `expense_categories` ⨝ `categories` (1:1 per receipt).

- Service: `src/lib/services/ExpenseService.ts`. `Expense` interface at line 22; the join query is `buildExpenseQuery()` at `ExpenseService.ts:154-190` — PostgREST embed `receipts → expense_categories (category_id, categorization_source) → categories (name, color)`.

- Migration `010_expense_categorization.sql` documents the design ("Expenses are derived views from receipts, not separate entities").

## 4. Transactions

**Table** `transactions` — `supabase/migrations/007_transactions_table.sql:2-15`. Model: `src/lib/models/Transaction.ts:3` (`TransactionRow`).

Key fields:
- `id` uuid PK
- `family_id` uuid NOT NULL → `families(id)` ON DELETE CASCADE (transactions are **family-scoped**, not user-scoped)
- `transaction_date` date NOT NULL
- `vendor_name` text NOT NULL
- `amount` numeric NOT NULL (no sign constraint in schema; stored as-is from CSV import)
- `credit_card_type` text NOT NULL (enum in `Transaction.ts:33` — PC Financial, Amex, RBC, TD, Simplii, EQ, Wealth Simple)
- `excluded` boolean NOT NULL default false — originally named `ignored`, renamed in `012_rename_ignored_to_excluded.sql`; means "excluded from reconciliation"
- `created_at`, `updated_at` timestamptz
- A `status` CHECK was added in `20260111000004_add_status_check_to_transactions.sql`
- Unique index on `(family_id, transaction_date, vendor_name, amount, credit_card_type)` created in `007` but later **dropped** in `20260419_drop_transactions_unique_index.sql`

**Matching to receipts:** the link lives on the receipt side — `receipts.matched_transaction_id` uuid → `transactions(id)` ON DELETE SET NULL (`008_add_receipt_transaction_matching.sql`).

## 5. Categories & expense_categories

Both defined in `supabase/migrations/010_expense_categorization.sql`:

`categories` (line 26): `id` PK, `user_id` NOT NULL→auth.users, `name` varchar(100) NOT NULL, `color` varchar(7) nullable, timestamps. Unique on `(user_id, lower(name))`. (Later migrated to family-scope by `20260111000001_migrate_categories_to_family_scope.sql`; test `CategoryRow` uses `family_id`.)

`expense_categories` (line 48) — the join table, **PK is `receipt_id`** (enforces 1:1 receipt↔category):
- `receipt_id` uuid PK → `receipts(id)` ON DELETE CASCADE
- `category_id` uuid → `categories(id)` ON DELETE SET NULL (nullable)
- `categorization_source` varchar(10) NOT NULL CHECK in `('manual','auto')`
- timestamps

`vendor_category_rules` (line 68): `user_id`, `vendor_pattern`, `category_id` — auto-categorization rules.

**How a receipt gets categorized:** `ExpenseService.assignCategory(receiptId, categoryId, source)` (`ExpenseService.ts:240`) does an `upsert` into `expense_categories` with `onConflict: 'receipt_id'` (manual overrides auto). Auto-assignment path: `ReceiptService.ts:368` calls `expenseService.assignCategory(receipt.id, vendorRule.category_id, 'auto')` when a vendor rule matches. No models file for these; row types only in `testDatabase.ts` (`CategoryRow`, `VendorCategoryRuleRow`).

**No production seed data mechanism exists.**
- `supabase/config.toml:58-63` declares `[db.seed] sql_paths = ["./seed.sql"]`, but **`supabase/seed.sql` does not exist** (default template config, unused).
- No `seed`/`sample`/`demo`/`fixture` npm script in `package.json` (scripts are only dev/build/test/lint).
- Fixtures found are all **test-only / unit-test scoped**, not DB seeders:

  - `src/lib/tests/builders/testDatabase.ts` (hand-written typed schema for integration tests — types families/family_members/receipts/categories but inserts nothing by itself)
  - `src/lib/utils/receiptDateCorrection.fixtures.ts`, `src/lib/components/DataTableFixture.svelte`, `e2e/demo.test.ts`, `src/demo.spec.ts`
- No test factory that seeds real families/receipts into a running DB; tests use the Supabase mock or the in-memory typed client.

## 7. Real signup flow & how a family is created

There is **no signup/register route** — only login. `src/routes/login/+page.svelte:17` calls `supabase.auth.signInWithPassword(...)`; there's no `+page.server.ts` and no `signUp()` call anywhere in `src/`. (Users appear to be provisioned externally / invite-based.)

Family creation is **lazy and DB-driven**, not done in an app route:
- Trigger function `set_receipt_family_id()` (`20251010...:149`) fires before insert on `receipts`; if `family_id` is null it calls `ensure_default_family()`.
- `ensure_default_family()` (SECURITY DEFINER; `005_fix_ensure_default_family_service_role.sql:5` and `20251010...:159`): finds the caller's active default membership; if none, **inserts a new `families` row (`created_by = uid`) and a `family_members` row (`role='owner', status='active', is_default=true`)**. This is the single place a family + membership get created.
- Ties to `auth.users`: `family_members.user_id` FK → `auth.users(id)`; the function keys everything off `auth.uid()` (or `request.jwt.claims->>'sub'` when invoked via the service-role RPC `insert_receipt_with_context`, `003`/`20260717`).
- Default categories seeded per-user via `create_default_categories(p_user_id)` (`010_...`) — a SECURITY DEFINER function, not wired to an auth trigger in these migrations.

## 8. RLS

RLS is enabled on all domain tables and is **family-membership scoped, keyed on `auth.uid()`** (plus legacy user_id scoping on categories/vendor_rules).

- **receipts:** RLS enabled in `001_init.sql:19`. Original policies were `user_id = auth.uid()`; hardened to family-scoped in `20260717_security_remediation_chain.sql` — insert/update policies now require `EXISTS(family_members fm WHERE fm.family_id = receipts.family_id AND fm.user_id = auth.uid())` (fixing a tautological check; lines 85-130), with a `family_id IS NULL AND auth.uid()=user_id` fallback.
- **transactions:** `007_transactions_table.sql:20-71` — all four policies gated on `EXISTS(family_members fm WHERE fm.family_id = transactions.family_id AND fm.user_id = auth.uid())`.
- **families / family_members:** policies in `20251010...:306-380`; recursion issues fixed by `20260113_fix_family_members_recursion.sql`, `20260114_simple_family_members_policy.sql`, and `20260717_...` (R5/F1) which replaced world-readable policies with membership-scoped SELECT via a SECURITY DEFINER helper and removed the open self-insert policy. Member listing goes through `get_family_members()` RPC (`20260719_get_family_members_rpc.sql`).
- **categories / expense_categories / vendor_category_rules:** RLS in `010_expense_categorization.sql:88-104` — `categories`/`vendor_rules` use `auth.uid() = user_id`; `expense_categories` uses `receipt_id IN (SELECT id FROM receipts WHERE user_id = auth.uid())`. RLS re-scoped by `20260111000001/2/3` (family-scope migrations, incl. `20260111000003_fix_expense_categories_rls.sql`).
- **Storage (`receipts` bucket):** `20260225_secure_receipts_storage.sql` makes the bucket private; SELECT allows any active family member to read files owned by a co-member (owner uid = first path segment), while INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE remain restricted to the owner's own `{auth.uid()}/` folder.
- Additional lockdown: `20260717_security_remediation_chain.sql` and `20260718_fix_f3_revoke_anon.sql` (revokes anon access).

**Key policy files:** `001_init.sql`, `007_transactions_table.sql`, `010_expense_categorization.sql`, `20251010000319_remote_schema.sql`, `20260111000003_fix_expense_categories_rls.sql`, `20260113_fix_family_members_recursion.sql`, `20260114_simple_family_members_policy.sql`, `20260225_secure_receipts_storage.sql`, `20260717_security_remediation_chain.sql`, `20260718_fix_f3_revoke_anon.sql`, `20260719_get_family_members_rpc.sql`.

That last point creates the first real fork.

---

**Question 1 — Who actually consumes this sample data?**

You said "for testing and also for documentation screenshots/videos." But those two want very different things here:

- **Screenshots/videos** need data sitting in a *real database that a running dev app can log into* and render — realistic, varied, visually rich.
- **Automated testing** in this repo runs against *in-memory/mock clients*, never a real DB. A DB seed does nothing for the existing unit/Playwright suites.

- **(A)** Manual / exploratory testing + screenshots — i.e. *"I want to log in as a demo user in the real running app and see a fully-populated family."* One mechanism, seeds a real DB. **← my recommendation**
- **(B)** Feeding the automated test suites (would require first building the missing auth/seed harness — much bigger scope).
- **(C)** Both, explicitly — build the seed now, and design it so a future automated harness can reuse it.

My recommendation is **(A)**: a single seed that populates a real database with a "Sample Family" you can log into. It directly serves screenshots/videos and manual testing today, and doesn't drag in the much larger job of wiring a real-DB automated harness. Which do you want?
C) However we're not writing the test harness today.

**Question 2 — The auth user behind the sample family.**

A family is worthless without a login, and `family_members.user_id` is a hard FK to `auth.users`. So the seed must be tied to at least one auth user. Options:

- **(A)** Create a **dedicated demo auth user** with fixed, known credentials (e.g. `demo@yfl.example` / a fixed password), created via the Supabase Admin API (service-role). The seed owns this user end-to-end — you log in as them for screenshots, and it's disposable/re-creatable. **← my recommendation**
- **(B)** Graft the sample family onto **your own real account** (`mark@agilepainrelief.com`). No new user, but it pollutes your real account with fake receipts/transactions and is awkward to clean up.
- **(C)** Attach to an **existing test user** if one already exists in the remote project.

Since you want this for public-facing docs/screenshots and want it disposable and reusable, **(A) a dedicated `demo@…` user** is cleanest — no pollution of your real data, a stable login you can hand to a future test harness, and trivial teardown (delete the user → cascade wipes their receipts, and we clean the family).

One catch to flag: a dedicated demo user means the seed **must** run with the **service-role key** (to create the auth user and bypass RLS). That's a secret you'd run locally, never ship to the browser. Are you good with **(A) a dedicated demo user via service-role**?
A) and in fact we need two test users - so we have a family.

Two demo users, one shared family — good, that also lets screenshots show the "family members see each other's receipts" feature.

**Question 3 — Which database does the seed target?**

This is a safety fork. Screenshots need a *running dev app*, and this app's dev server reads `PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL` from `.env` — which points at the **linked remote production project** (`YFL Expense Tracker`, ca-central-1). There's also the option of the local Supabase stack (`supabase db reset` / `supabase start`).

Fully isolated — no fake data ever touches production, service-role key is the throwaway local one, teardown is `supabase db reset`. Downside: you run `supabase start` and switch env to the local URL when you want the demo. **← my recommendation**

Cleanup must be surgical, and any RLS mistake is a production mistake.
- **(C)** Support **both** via a target flag, defaulting to local.

I recommend **(A) local stack**. Fake demo data in production is the kind of thing that's easy to create and painful to fully remove, and a demo user with a known password living in prod is a standing liability. Local isolation gives you a clean, resettable environment purpose-built for screenshots and a future test harness.

The tradeoff is the env switch. Do you want **(A) local**, or is the env-switching friction enough that you'd rather **(B) remote** (accepting the prod-pollution risk), or **(C) both with a flag**?

# Backlog

The single working list — features, UX bugs, engineering, open questions, and
refactoring. Refactoring items are summarized here as one-liners; the full
detail (smell, effort, sibling sites, plan) lives in
[Refactoring backlog](refactoring-backlog.md), which is a reference, not a
separate to-do list.

## Features

- **Spending Report (v1).** New top-level `/spending` tab rolling up Expenses by Importance → Grouping → Category, months across, "Year to Date" total. Adds `importance_areas` + `category_groups` tables (Importance attaches to the Grouping) and `categories.group_id`, seeded from `docs/SampleHierachy.txt`. Client-side pure aggregation (`buildSpendingReport`), view-only, no editing UI. Uncategorized bucket included in Grand Total; refunds (negative amounts) net against spend. **Chart view (v0.60):** `Table | Chart` toggle adds a LayerChart stacked bar (bar per Grouping, stacked by month, sequential ramp; Importance as sub-label; click a bar to drill to Categories, breadcrumb back). Pure `buildSpendingChart`; render-tested. **Table cell drill-down (v0.55) ✅ DONE:** clicking a non-blank table cell opens `/expenses` filtered to exactly what it sums — category×month, category YTD, Grouping/Importance subtotals (expanded to member category ids), Uncategorized (`filter=uncategorized`), and Grand Total (date range only, ties out incl. Uncategorized). Pure `buildSpendingDrilldownParams` (8 tests); report rows/sections now carry ids (`categoryId`/group `id`/importance `id`). **Editable hierarchy — assign & re-parent (v0.65) ✅ DONE:** an **Edit hierarchy** page at `/spending/hierarchy` (button on `/spending`) lets the maintainer assign a Category to a Grouping (or Uncategorized) and move a Grouping to another Importance — closing the "custom/renamed categories stuck in Uncategorized" gap without SQL. Pure `buildHierarchyTree` (8 tests) + presentational `HierarchyEditor.svelte` (5 render tests); `CategoryService.assignCategoryToGroup` / `moveGroupToImportance`. Unassigned bucket surfaced up top. **Assign-on-create (v0.66) ✅ DONE:** the inline "Create new category…" form (expenses page `CategoryDropdown`) offers an optional Group selector so a new category is filed into a Grouping at birth instead of Uncategorized (`createCategory` gained an optional `groupId`; selector hidden when no groups passed, so receipt/reconciliation dropdowns are unchanged). **Historical-year expense upload (built, pending release) ✅ DONE:** an **Import Expenses** page at `/expenses/import` (buttons on `/expenses` and `/spending`) imports historical Expenses from CSV/XLS/XLSX (columns `Timestamp, Merchant, Amount, Category`; `Tag` ignored; Amount keeps its sign so refunds net). Each row → an imageless `receipts` row (no schema change — `receipt_image_path` nullable, `suspicious_date` false) + an `expense_categories` link; new category names are auto-created (land Uncategorized, warned in the preview). Two-step **preview → confirm** with count-based dedup (`date|merchant|amount|category`) so re-import is a no-op. Pure `parseExpenseImportCsv` (14) + `computeExpenseImportPlan`/`buildExpenseCategoryLinks` (12) + `ExpenseImportService` (7); the bank-parser CSV primitives were extracted to `csvPrimitives.ts` (base delegates; 229 parser tests unchanged). This **unblocks** prior-period overlay + year-over-year. Deferred: **chart-bar drill-down** (same affordance on the chart bars — carry the cell-link into `/expenses` from a bar/bracket click); **hierarchy tier CRUD** (create/rename/delete/reorder Groupings + Importance areas, with cascade-delete confirmations); prior-period overlay + year-over-year (now unblocked), quarter/period selection, multi-chart menu, export. See [Spending Report design](plans/2026-07-09-spending-report-design.md).
- **Delete a category (built, pending release) ✅ DONE.** Each category row in the hierarchy editor (`/spending/hierarchy`) now has a **Delete** button (`HierarchyEditor.onDeleteCategory`). # Demo Data Seed

A re-runnable script that populates a self-contained **"Sample Family (DEMO)"**
in the **remote** Supabase project, so the running app can be logged into for
documentation screenshots/videos and manual exploratory testing.

It is deliberately **image-free**: every seeded receipt has
`receipt_image_path = null`, so receipts render in their placeholder state
("No image" / "(manual)"). See the note on that below.

> **Reuse:** the seed is written so a future automated test harness can reuse
> the same fixtures. That harness is **not** built yet — this is a dev utility
> today.

## Logins

| Role   | Email                        |
| ------ | ---------------------------- |
| Owner  | `sample.parent@example.com`  |
| Member | `sample.partner@example.com` |

Both share one family and one **randomly generated password**, printed to the
console at the end of each seed run (nothing memorable is left standing in the
project). Copy it from the run output. `@example.com` is an IANA-reserved
documentation domain — it accepts no mail and can't collide with real accounts.

## Commands

```bash
npm run seed:demo            # auto-clean any prior demo data, then rebuild
npm run seed:demo:teardown   # delete the demo users + demo family
```

Both wrap `op run --env-file=.env -- tsx …`, so the required env is pulled from
1Password just like `npm run dev`. They need:

- `PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL` — the target project (echoed on start).
- `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` — full-access secret; required to create the auth
  users (Admin API) and to insert RLS-protected rows. The scripts hard-fail with
  a clear message if either is missing.

`seed:demo` is **auto-clean-then-recreate**: it runs the teardown first, so every
run yields the same known-good state. Deletion is scoped strictly to the two
demo emails and the `Sample Family (DEMO)` name, so it can only ever touch demo
artifacts — never your real data (which lives under a different `family_id` and
stays invisible to the demo login via RLS, and vice-versa).

## What it creates

- **Two auth users** (owner + member), one shared **family**, with the app's own
  **default categories + spending hierarchy** (via the `create_default_categories`
  and `create_default_hierarchy` RPCs) so the demo matches a real new family.
- **~150 receipts** spread across **all of 2025 + Jan–Jul 2026**, ~6–8 per month,
  split across both users and most of the 13 default groupings / 3 Areas of
  Importance — enough to fill the Spending grid, YTD, and the compare-to-prior-year
  toggle.
- **~95 transactions**, most matched 1:1 to a receipt (equal amount, date within
  3 days), the rest unmatched on each side.
- **One instance of every notable edge state**, planted in recent months so it's
  visible without scrolling: split receipt, matched pair, unmatched (both sides),
  duplicate pair, suspicious/old date, future-dated ("Upcoming"), refund/credit,
  excluded transaction, amount-not-read (null total), foreign currency (USD), and
  uncategorized.

The dataset is generated deterministically (fixed RNG seed), so reseeding
produces the same data and screenshots stay stable.

## The no-image consequence

Because no receipt has an image, every screen shows its empty/placeholder state:
the Expenses page shows a column of grey "No image" boxes, the Receipts page has
blank thumbnail cells, and Reconciliation tags every receipt "(manual)". This is
intentional. If a screenshot ever needs the receipt-image viewer itself, seed a
few receipts with real placeholder images (a small change to `scripts/demo/data.ts`).

## Files

- `scripts/demo/common.ts` — env guard, service-role client, teardown.
- `scripts/demo/data.ts` — pure, deterministic dataset generator (no DB access).
- `scripts/demo/seed.ts` — orchestrates users → family → categories → data.
- `scripts/demo/teardown.ts` — standalone teardown entrypoint.

Run via `tsx` (added as a dev dependency).
